description: How a built-in function a formula passes as a value is stored, and what decides it. Formulas were given to Excel through Range.Formula2 in fresh workbooks, one workbook per question so that a name one formula introduced could not capture the next, then saved and the stored <f> text read out of the package. Excel prefixes the name with _xleta. and uppercases it in every position it was given one; it leaves the name bare where it names a sheet, and where a defined name spelled like the function is visible from the formula (a workbook-level name, or one scoped to the formula's own sheet). A name scoped to another sheet does not capture it, but Range.Formula still reports the prefix while any name of that spelling exists.
probe: one-off COM scripts (Workbooks.Add, Names.Add, Range.Formula2, SaveAs as .xlsx and .xlsb); tools/excel-oracle/run.ts --xlsx on this library's package and on a control
openClass: headless COM (DisplayAlerts off) for the saves; run.ts opens read-only and reports no repair for both packages below

classification.method: one cell =MAP(1,<name>) per name, in a fresh workbook with no defined names, for the [MS-XLS] function table, the future-function registry, the Analysis ToolPak functions and every member of Application.WorksheetFunction (with _ read as .)
bare: the XLM macro functions of the [MS-XLS] table (GOTO, HALT, GET.CELL, ... 116 names)
classification.xlsb: the binary save registers each prefixed name and parameter as a BrtName (_xleta.SUM, _xlpm.x) without the function flag, with target #NAME?

writtenByThisLibrary.what: the fixture's names and typed formulas authored through the model, written with fullCalcOnLoad

controlWithoutThePrefix.what: the same package with every _xleta. removed from its parts
